methodology: The decomposition process involves breaking down the research topic and the generated specification into independent, technically specific, and implementable units. The criteria for each unit are: 1. Independence: Each unit should represent a single, self-contained requirement or feature. 2. Technical Specificity: Each unit should be unambiguous and clearly define a specific aspect of the design. 3. Implementability: Each unit should be directly translatable into a design element or constraint. The approach involves reading each document, identifying key requirements, features, and constraints, and then formulating them as atomic units. For the research topic, the units are derived from the problem description and the provided Rule 110 definition. For the generated specification, the units are extracted from the provided JSON structure, focusing on the combinational logic, boundary conditions, and load functionality.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The system consists of a one-dimensional array of 512 cells (q[511:0]).
Each cell can be either on (1) or off (0).
The state of the entire system advances by one time step on each clock cycle.
The next state of each cell q[i] depends on its current state and the states of its two neighbors, q[i-1] and q[i+1], according to the Rule 110 table.
Boundary cells q[0] and q[511] should consider their non-existent neighbors q[-1] and q[512] to be off (0).
A synchronous active-high load input allows initializing the state of the system.
When the load input is asserted, the state of the system is loaded with the data provided on the data[511:0] input.
spec_atomic_units: The module `top_module` implements a 512-cell Rule 110 cellular automaton.
The module has a clock input `clk`.
The module has a synchronous active-high load input `load`.
The module has a 512-bit data input `data`.
The module has a 512-bit output `q` representing the state of the cells.
The output `q` updates on the rising edge of `clk`.
When `load` is high, `q` is updated with the value of `data` on the rising edge of `clk`.
When `load` is low, `q` is updated with the next state of the cellular automaton, calculated based on the current state of `q` and the Rule 110 logic, on the rising edge of `clk`.
The core combinational logic implements Rule 110 for each of the 512 cells.
For each cell `q[i]`, its next state `next_q[i]` is determined by the current states of its left neighbor `left`, itself `center`, and its right neighbor `right`.
The boundary conditions dictate that `q[-1]` and `q[512]` are always zero.
The combinational logic for each cell can be expressed as: `next_q[i] = (!left & center & right) | (!left & center & !right) | (!left & !center & right) | (left & center & !right)`.
This can be simplified to `next_q[i] = (center & (right | !left)) | (!left & !center & right)`.
This logic is replicated 512 times, once for each cell.
The `load` signal acts as a selector.
When `load` is asserted (high), the output `q[i]` is directly driven by `data[i]`.
When `load` is deasserted (low), the output `q[i]` is driven by `next_q[i]`.
This selection is implemented using a multiplexer for each cell: `q[i] = load ? data[i] : next_q[i]`.
The complete combinational logic consists of 512 instances of Rule 110 logic and 512 2-to-1 multiplexers.
The next state of `q` depends on the current state of `q` and the combinational logic implementing Rule 110.
The critical path is from `q` through the Rule 110 combinational logic back to `q` via the non-blocking assignment within the `always @(posedge clk)` block.
The setup time for `data` with respect to `clk` when `load` is asserted must be met.
The setup time for the signals that determine the next state of `q` (based on the current `q` and Rule 110) with respect to `clk` when `load` is deasserted must also be met.
The circuit is a sequential circuit with 512 registers (q[511:0]).
The registers are updated on the positive edge of the clock (`posedge clk`).
The update is done using a non-blocking assignment (`<=`).
The `q` signal is declared as a `reg`, indicating that its value is stored between clock cycles.
The `always @(posedge clk)` block describes the synchronous behavior of the circuit.
When `load` is high, the registers are loaded with the value of `data`.
When `load` is low, the registers are updated with the next state of the cellular automaton based on Rule 110.
The boundary conditions (q[-1] and q[512] are zero) are handled implicitly within the combinational logic that implements Rule 110.
